columns.headline: Brad Buries Jared, Kris Benches His Way Out of a Win
columns.dek: Brad posted the week's high score by a mile, Kris lost the closest game with the winning lineup on his bench, and Jon took first place while losing.
body: Brad hung 147.14 on Jared, the high score of the week and the biggest beating, a 69.76-point margin that pushes the series to 15-4. His best possible lineup was 150.04, the best of the week, and he left only 2.90 on the bench, which means Brad set a lineup like a man who reads. Brad would like it noted that his head is not that big and nothing else is that small, and on Sunday the scoreboard sided with the second claim. Jared, meanwhile, started Bijan Robinson for 6.30 against a 21.34 projection and fielded a bench of Lamar Jackson, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Travis Etienne Jr. that laid three straight donuts. He drops two spots to 11th at 3-9.

The closest game was Ben 83.72, Kris 82.10, a 1.62-point loss Kris chose for himself. His best lineup was worth 88.30, enough to win, because he benched Woody Marks and his 9.10 to start Rhamondre Stevenson in the flex for 3.60. Kris slides from third to fourth and Ben now leads the series 9-7. Ben also cleared the median of 83.65 by 0.07, which is exactly the amount by which Joe K missed it.

That would be the Joe K who lost to Jeff 100.30 to 83.58 after Patrick Mahomes put up 10.48 against an 18.77 projection. His backup quarterbacks, Bo Nix and Jacoby Brissett, scored 4.48 and a donut, so even the insurance policy was dumb. He falls from seventh to ninth at 5-7. Jeff won despite himself: C.J. Stroud's 22.98 sat on his bench and he started Terry McLaurin for 3.20 over Jakobi Meyers and his 10.80, leaving 15.48 on the pine. Jeff now leads that series 12-8.

Family business was a split decision. Joe G beat Collin 78.66 to 69.14 with the tenth-best score of the week, below the median, while Mark Andrews contributed 0.90 from the flex. The older brother is supposed to know better, and instead he won with the kind of score that usually gets a man roasted in this column. Little brother Chad scored more, 83.24, and lost to Flanders anyway, with Kyren Williams posting 8.20 against a 19.17 projection and Stefon Diggs benched for 13.40 while Wan'Dale Robinson started in the flex for 3.70. Chad tumbles from first to second, though his 744.80 points for still lead the league.

Collin took the low score at 69.14 and benched Tyler Shough's 26.96 while Jordan Love started at quarterback for 20.24. To be fair to nobody, his best lineup of 77.16 still loses, so the bench was not the problem; the roster is. He sits alone in last at 2-10. Flanders was the week's big climber, posting the second-best score at 104.50 and jumping three spots from 11th to eighth behind Germie Bernard's 20.20 against a 7.79 projection, a win that came despite a donut from Will Shipley in the flex and Romeo Doubs left on the bench for 10.70 while Denzel Boston started for 2.00.

TJ beat Jon 101.60 to 95.42 on the best start of the week against projection: Tre Tucker, 24.20 on an 8.59 projection. TJ also started Roman Wilson, projected for nothing, and got exactly that, and Derrick Henry chipped in 4.50 on a 17.60 projection; dumb, but it worked, and TJ climbs to third at 8-4. Jon still leads the series 5-2 and, despite losing, beat the median with the fifth-best score and climbed into first alone at 9-3. Juwan Johnson and Antonio Williams both laid donuts in his lineup, which is the Jon experience in one week: a big production budget, two empty frames, and somehow it still ends up on top.

columns.headline: Chad Flattens Joe G and Takes Over First Place
columns.dek: Chad posted the week's best score by a mile, Jon won with the tenth-best score and still slid out of first, and Collin left a winning quarterback on the bench.
body: Chad did not so much beat Joe G as file a noise complaint against him. The final was 155.24 to 68.26, a margin of 86.98, the highest and lowest scores of the week in the same box. Jahmyr Gibbs put up 35.20 and Christian Watson beat his projection by 17.78. The series now sits tied 11-11, and Chad leads the standings at 8-2, ahead of Jon on points. Even his worst lineup call was a rounding error: 1.40 points left on the bench.

Joe G, meanwhile, got 1.90 from CeeDee Lamb on a 15.46 projection, and RJ Harvey chipped in 0.70. His best possible lineup was 81.36, so no bench move was saving this one. He drops from third to fifth at 6-4, which is still a winning record, which is the nicest thing anyone can say about his Sunday.

Now the one that hurts. Collin lost the week's closest game to Jon, 81.54 to 74.42, by 7.12. He started Tyler Shough at quarterback, who finished at -0.16 on a 16.51 projection, while Jordan Love sat on his bench with 25.28. Collin's best lineup was 107.46, enough to win, which makes him the only loser this week who chose his loss. He left 33.04 on the pine and slides to last at 2-8.

Jon will take the win, and he should, because it was a heist. His 81.54 was tenth of 12, well under the 100.25 median, and his bench produced exactly 0.00. Parker Washington's 27.40 carried the lineup. Jon went 1-1 on the week, and he slid from first to second at 8-2, behind Chad on points. Jon leads that series 4-3.

Jeff beat Brad 108.36 to 100.70 despite starting a quarterback who scored 0.00 on an 18.17 projection, with C.J. Stroud and his 20.94 sitting on the bench. Jayden Daniels and his 32.26 covered for it. Jeff jumps from ninth to sixth. Brad got 26.90 from Isaiah Likely and 1.10 from Carnell Tate, beat the 100.25 median by 0.45, and still lost. He stays eighth and still leads Jeff 10-7 in the series, for what that is worth this week.

TJ owns the start of the week: Drake Maye put up 39.46 on an 18.47 projection, beating it by 20.99, and TJ beat Ben 123.56 to 99.80. Ben missed the median by 0.45, got 1.10 from David Montgomery, and fell from seventh to tenth. Joe K handled Kris 124.88 to 105.50 and climbed from tenth to seventh. Kris left MarShawn Lloyd's 16.20 on the bench, but his best lineup was 124.00, still short, so blame the opponent and not the clipboard.

Down in the cellar, Flanders beat Jared 96.34 to 85.92 while getting 0.00 from tight end Kenyon Sadiq, and that was enough to climb out of last to eleventh. Jared got 1.50 from Deebo Samuel Sr. and fell from sixth to ninth. Jared still leads that series 9-8.
